findings.summary: SOL1-5 is only partly fixed. H1's row check lets `current` end with a newline and then only requires an equal newline count, so a proposed text can move that newline inside the row and rewrite the next (BROKER) row. H3's bullet-only check accepts a heading or a table inside an appended bullet. README lines 36-40 claim H1 'cannot add a row, a column or a heading' and that for H3 'no heading can be added'.
findings.evidence:
Mutations run with check_record on the published record and the pinned HS43 bytes, with E3 re-rendered. Accepted: H1 current = published current + '
' (it occurs once, because the OBSERVER line ends there) and proposed = published proposed minus its final ' |' + '
| INJECTED '. Same newline count, same unescaped '|' count. The applied text then has the line '| INJECTED | BROKER | 0 | CAP_NET_ADMIN, ...', so the BROKER row's cells shift. Also accepted: H3 appending '- ## 4.9 Injected heading in a list item
', '  ## 4.9 Injected indented heading
' (an ATX heading inside the list item in CommonMark) and '- x
  | a | b |
  |---|---|
'. Cause: line 267 tests '
' not in current.rstrip('
'), and line 273 compares newline counts, not zero. Lines 277-279 test only the '- ' or '  ' prefix of each line. Only the author-set effective digest stops such a record in check(). The published bytes are correct. Refused, correctly: H1 plus a new row, H1 with an injected '## 99.' line, H1 with an extra cell, H1 in the SERVER row, H3 rewrite, prepend or appended '### 4.9' heading. Fix: for row items, require no '
' in current or proposed. For H3, refuse appended lines whose content after the bullet or indent starts with '#' or '|', or soften README lines 36-40.

findings.summary: H1 says that among AF_UNIX sockets 'SELinux does' hold the listener to I01's path. Under matrix v5, SELinux bounds who may connect into the observer and which pathname socket file it may create. It does not bound where the observer listens. The README (lines 80-82) words this correctly; H1 overstates it.
findings.evidence: selinux_matrix_v3.allowed gives planeon_observer_t create, bind, listen and accept on unix_stream_socket planeon_observer_t with no path condition, and connectto only to planeon_server_t. allowed(planeon_observer_t, planeon_run_t, sock_file, create) is False in all three states, so a pathname socket in /run/planeon needs the named type transition W03 adds. An abstract-namespace name creates no sock_file; this is the reviewer's reading, because net/unix is not in the research tree. So the observer can listen elsewhere, but only the server can reach it. Suggest: 'SELinux bounds it: only the server may connect, and the socket file's type comes from W03's named rule'.

findings.summary: The stale-path route (O-W03-OBSERVER-UNIT, O-T04-HS53) is achievable under matrix v5 but leaves three details implicit. (a) It depends on W03's named type transition for policy-observer.sock, which T04 does not check. (b) The held directory descriptor covers fstatat and unlinkat but not bind, which resolves the pathname again. (c) On aarch64 there is no `unlink` syscall.
findings.evidence: (a) Matrix v5 has four typeTransitions and none for the observer's or broker's socket file. Its README (Objects on tmpfs) leaves those rules to W03. Without that rule the socket would be created as planeon_run_t. The observer has no sock_file create on planeon_run_t, so this fails closed, but the route's grants (sock_file getattr and unlink on planeon_observer_sock_t) only apply once the rule exists. A T04 check that the I01 socket file carries planeon_observer_sock_t would close this. (b) v6.12 <research>/net/socket.c:1857-1876 shows bind(fd, sockaddr, addrlen) with no directory descriptor. HE-004-I01 could confirm after bind that the socket sits in the held directory. (c) <research>/scripts/syscall.tbl lists unlinkat (35) and no unlink, so 'still killing unlink and unlinkat' applies only to unlinkat on aarch64. Verified: the v5 OBSERVER programs kill unlink, unlinkat, umask, fchmod, fchmodat and accept on both architectures. None of these is in the closed table.

accept4 in v6.12 <research>/net/socket.c: SYSCALL_DEFINE4(accept4, ..., int, flags) at 2030-2034; EINVAL for flags outside SOCK_CLOEXEC|SOCK_NONBLOCK at 1982-1983; plain accept passes flags 0 (2036-2040). include/linux/net.h:48,80-83: SOCK_CLOEXEC = O_CLOEXEC, SOCK_NONBLOCK = O_NONBLOCK under #ifndef ARCH_HAS_SOCKET_TYPES. include/uapi/asm-generic/fcntl.h:39 gives O_NONBLOCK 00004000 and :63 gives O_CLOEXEC 02000000. arm64 uapi asm/fcntl.h:23-26 overrides only O_DIRECTORY, O_NOFOLLOW, O_DIRECT and O_LARGEFILE. x86 has no uapi asm/fcntl.h in the tree. Numbers match the tables: bind 49/200, listen 50/201, accept4 288/242.

Seccomp limit: bind(int fd, sockaddr*, int) and listen(int fd, int) carry no family (net/socket.c:1857-1914), so the 'no descriptor family' statement is correct. __sys_listen_socket (1883-1895) calls security_socket_listen (1891) and never security_socket_bind (bind's hook is at 1840).

Not checkable in the research tree (no security/, net/ipv4/ or net/unix/): the AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET to unix_stream_socket mapping, the name_bind exemptions, the TCP autobind on listen, AF_UNIX bind umask and abstract names. All are stated as the author's reading or as T04 questions. The SEQPACKET mapping matches the reviewer's reading, and matrix v5 already relies on it for I05/I07.

TCP boundary: the v5 OBSERVER socket rule admits only AF_INET/AF_INET6 SOCK_STREAM with protocol 0 or 6 (CLOEXEC/NONBLOCK masked) and AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET. There is no io_uring call and no AF_NETLINK. Every listen reaches security_socket_listen, so O-W03-OBSERVER-TCP (no tcp_socket listen, no node_bind) closes listen-with-bind, port 0 and in-range binds and listen without bind. O-T04-HS53 tests all three cases on AF_INET and AF_INET6. O-MATRIX-OBSERVER-TCP adds the data closure. Matrix v5 closes the observer's name_bind (source closure; no port grants it), and its README:234 states the range part. Residual R-OBSERVER-TCP-LISTEN is complete for the observer's own sockets.

Socket file and directory under matrix v5, all three states: planeon_observer_t has dir search, getattr, open, read, add_name, remove_name and write on planeon_run_t, and sock_file getattr, unlink, create, setattr and write on planeon_observer_sock_t. init_t has dir create, rmdir and remove_name on planeon_run_t but no getattr or unlink on planeon_observer_sock_t. planeon_server_t has no remove_name. broker, gate and maint cannot unlink planeon_observer_sock_t. Each socket-file type gives WRITE only to its listener and connector, so notAmended's note on the I05/I07/I02 sockets holds. Route (a) (fstatat AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW, refuse a non-socket, unlinkat on the held dirfd, bind) is achievable before the filter, and the steady-state filter adds no unlink, umask, fchmod or fchmodat. The fallback O-MATRIX-OBSERVER-SOCK-CLEAR grants nothing now. systemd's handling of the shared RuntimeDirectory= is a stated T04 question. W01 §5.3 'after own seal step' and native profile v3 do not require a pre-exec filter.

Shared directory: I07 is /run/planeon/maintenance/policy-write.sock (HS43 spec :147, i07 README :33), so /run/planeon/live-proxy/ holds exactly the I01, I02 and I05 sockets: three listeners, as the obligations and T04 name them (SOL1-2 fixed).
